author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.
decisions:

  the way the project records non-goal changes.

The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected through a prefilled form reached by its address. The correction updates that visit in place under the booking rules and returns to the owner's record.
acceptance_criteria: Given a booked visit, when GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit is requested, then the existing visit form (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) is shown with the `visit` model attribute holding that visit's current date and description.
Given a booked visit, when a new description and a date later than today are POSTed to the same URL, then that visit is updated and the response redirects to the owner detail page.
Given a booked visit, when a correction is saved, then the pet's visit count is unchanged: the visit is updated in place, and no new visit record is added.
Given a blank description, when a correction is POSTed, then the form is redisplayed with the description field in error and the visit is unchanged.
Given a date of today or earlier, when a correction is POSTed, then the form is redisplayed with the date field in error and the visit is unchanged.
Given a visitId that does not belong to the named pet, or a pet that does not belong to the named owner, when the edit URL is requested or posted, then the request is refused and no visit changes.
non_goals: Any edit link or other visible entry point on the owner detail page; the owner deferred it to a follow-up request.
Correcting a visit to a past date; a correction follows the booking rules (recorded as an Open Question).
notes: Owner decisions quoted from intake line 1. PRD: Visits gains REQ-VIS-003 with four Done-when bullets and edge cases 3-4; NG-5 row narrowed to cancellation; two Open Questions added (past-date correction; owner-page entry point). New non-goal ADR docs/adr/2026-09-30-non-goal-visit-cancellation-only.md; the 2026-08-08 non-goal ADR status now points to it. docs/adr/README.md index needs the new row, which is outside this agent's write scope (system-design-expert or doc-sync). Edge case 3 (visit outside the named pet or owner) is the narrowest reading and extends Visits edge case 1; how the refusal is presented is a design choice. The edit form reuses the booking template, which shows the pet's earlier visits (REQ-VIS-002). This slice neither requires nor forbids that display. The booking-rules test is one data-driven test covering the blank-description and non-future-date cases.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction extends VisitController (system-design § Contracts) with the edit pattern PetController already shows for pets (optional path id on the @ModelAttribute loader, GET renders the shared form, POST validates then saves through OwnerRepository). One adjustment: the visit loader must branch on an optional visitId. With it, the loader returns the existing visit found owner -> pet -> visit instead of creating a new Visit and attaching it to the pet, which is what it does today for booking. Without the branch the correction would add a second visit. The lookup goes through the aggregate root (§ Contracts invariants: Owner is the entry point, no VisitRepository). Pet gains a find-visit-by-identity method mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer). The save stays on OwnerRepository.save(owner), which cascades the change. No new package, module, dependency, or ADR. Basis: grep and file reads of VisitController, PetController, Owner, Pet (IDE oracle not connected).
integration_points: Entry points GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit. Binding target: the persisted Visit that the loader resolves through owner -> pet, behind an allow-list of date and description (security-principles § Mass assignment). Keep the existing identifier disallow list alongside it. The allow-list applies to the controller's visit binder, so booking binds the same two fields.

Repository boundary (OwnerRepository): reuse the existing @MockitoBean stub in VisitControllerTests. Reason: OwnerRepository extends JpaRepository, so a hand-written double inside @WebMvcTest is impractical, and the existing class already stubs it (testing-principles § Mocking Policy, tolerated). Assert on the state of the real Owner/Pet/Visit graph the stub returns (visit count, edited fields), not on interaction verification alone.
Framework transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned harness (CLAUDE.md § Testing Strategy).

Rule reuse: the non-future-date rejection (field error code typeMismatch.visitDate) and @Valid bean validation apply identically on the correction POST. Extract the date check to one private method that both handlers call, and do not duplicate it.

patterns.description: findPet: @ModelAttribute loader with an optional path id, choosing between a new entity and the existing one reached through the owner
getPet(Integer id): lookup-by-identity inside the aggregate. Pet's visit lookup mirrors it
refusal of a pet outside the named owner via IllegalArgumentException (Visits edge case 1). A visitId outside the named pet is refused the same way (edge case 3), and nothing is saved

risks.risk: The loader today calls pet.addVisit(new Visit()) unconditionally. On the edit path this would attach a phantom new visit that the save then persists, breaking 'the pet gains no additional visit'.
risks.mitigation: Branch the loader on an optional visitId path variable, and add a new visit only when it is absent (system-design § Contracts invariants; PetController.findPet pattern). Test the visit count on the returned graph.

risks.risk: A failed validation must leave the visit unchanged, even though binding writes onto the loaded persisted Visit.
risks.mitigation: open-in-view is disabled (system-design § Persistence), so the loaded graph is detached and nothing persists without save. Return the form before any save on errors. The test asserts that save is never reached on the failure path.

risks.risk: Visit lookup scans one pet's visits. The design doc has no § Scale and Load section, so no row exists to cite.
risks.mitigation: The pet's visits are already loaded eagerly by the existing owner lookup, so no query is added. Size unrecorded, treated as bounded: simplest readable form (linear scan, as Owner.getPet does).

risks.risk: The template's submit label reads 'Add Visit' on a correction. A new label key must exist in all eleven bundles (REQ-LANG-002).
risks.mitigation: Narrowest reading: leave the label unchanged. The heading already drops 'New' for a persisted visit. If the implementer changes the label, reuse an existing bundle key rather than adding hard-coded text.

notes: ADR index: added the row for docs/adr/2026-09-30-non-goal-visit-cancellation-only.md and marked the 2026-08-08 row's NG-5 half as narrowed, relayed from the product expert. Contracts rows: REQ-VIS-003 joined Owner, Pet (purpose now names the visit lookup), Visit, OwnerRepository, VisitController (purpose now names correction). Brief defect for the owner: docs/system-design.md carries no § Scale and Load section (harness template predates it), so scaling paths cannot cite a row. The PRD's two open questions (past-date correction; owner-page entry point) are product-owned and need no design action. The narrowest reading holds: booking rules apply and no link is added. Refusal presentation for edge case 3 follows edge case 1 (exception to the error page). Whether refusals should become a 404 is not decided here. No design-doc-autofix records to audit.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Pet.getVisit(Integer) is a rule below the web boundary: docs/system-design.md line 90 assigns it to Pet ('owns its visits by cascade, finds one of them by identity'). It is exercised only through the WebMvcTest in VisitControllerTests. No unit test reaches it: `grep -rn -F 'getVisit(' src/test` returns nothing, and the test directory has no PetTests.java (OwnerTests.java exists for the sibling Owner.getPet). Its three decision paths (matching id returns the visit, unknown id returns null, an unsaved visit with a null id is skipped via !visit.isNew()) are therefore pinned only by framework-booted tests. The unsaved-visit guard is not reachable from the controller tests at all, so removing it would fail no test. Placement rule: a rule the design assigns below the boundary needs a unit test at that seam.

recommendations: Add a PetTests unit class with one test per Pet.getVisit path, named the{Subject}Should{Outcome}. Build pets through a named default or factory, not raw constructors with inline literals. Keep VisitControllerTests' one representative path for the edit route.

The 'visit is unchanged' half of Done-when bullet 4 is asserted only as verify(owners, never()).save(...), an interaction check. The loader returns the live Visit and the binder mutates it before validation, so the in-memory visit is changed after a refused correction. Nothing persists because save is never called. Consider asserting the visit's observable state where it is reachable, or recording why never-save is the contract.

Coverage-map shows declared test theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheBookingRulesAreBroken absent. It is split into two tests (blank description, non-future date), and the build-pass notes record the split. Coverage of Done-when bullets 1-4 and edge cases 3 and 4 is present. The declaration should be updated to the split names.

Not verified in this review: python3 scripts/changeset.py failed with 'base ref or working-tree snapshot unresolved', so I read the diff with `git diff -- src`. The jacoco coverage percentage was not read. ./gradlew test reported UP-TO-DATE and BUILD SUCCESSFUL.
approved_aspects: VisitControllerTests edit-route tests are straight-line, follow the BDD the{Subject}Should{Outcome} naming, and use AssertJ. The update test compares the whole expected Visit with usingRecursiveComparison.

Named constants (BOOKED_VISIT_ID, UNKNOWN_ID, CORRECTED_DESCRIPTION) and the createAVisit factory remove mystery literals. The outside-pet test is parameterized over both the unknown visit and the unknown pet.
MockMvc plus the existing @MockitoBean OwnerRepository follows the host-file idiom. No new mock framework stubs beyond the host file's pattern.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Mass assignment: VisitController.java:53 `dataBinder.setAllowedFields("date", "description");` keeps the persisted Visit loaded on the edit route to the two fields the form offers, and the existing `setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id")` at :54 stays. Because the @InitBinder names no attribute, the allow-list also covers the `@ModelAttribute Owner owner` bound on both POST handlers. That closes the pre-existing possibility of binding Owner/pet fields (for example `firstName`, `pets[0].name`) through the visit routes, so it strengthens the baseline rather than weakening it.

Ownership/IDOR: the loader resolves the visit through the owner->pet->visit chain on every request. It uses `Pet pet = owner.getPet(petId);` (VisitController.java:71) and then `Visit existingVisit = pet.getVisit(visitId);` (:80), which fails closed with IllegalArgumentException when a visit is outside the named pet. Pet.getVisit only returns persisted visits that belong to that pet (`!visit.isNew() && Objects.equals(visit.getId(), id)`). No cross-request state is trusted.

Validation parity: the edit POST carries `@Valid Visit visit` (Visit.description is `@NotBlank`), and it applies the same future-date rule as booking through the shared `rejectDateNotInFuture`. It saves only after `result.hasErrors()` is false.

Output escaping: the edit form reuses pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.html, which renders the description through th:field/th:text. `grep -rn -F -e utext src/main/resources/templates/` returned no hits. The form has no th:action, so it posts back to the request URL.

Error disclosure: the new exception message carries only the two integer path ids, the same pattern as the existing owner/pet messages. error.html:18 renders `${message}` escaped via th:text, and no secret or internal detail reaches it.

Surface: two routes are added (GET/POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit). Both are open like every other mutating route in the documented no-auth/no-CSRF demonstration baseline (docs/security-principles.md), and management exposure is unchanged. No query text, file/resource path, shell call, deserialization, logging, or credential is introduced in the diff.

Supply chain: build.gradle and pom.xml are unchanged in this change set (`git diff --stat HEAD -- build.gradle pom.xml` was empty). No NVD match ran, because dependencyCheck is not configured (`grep -F dependencyCheck build.gradle` returned no hits). The resolved versions are spring-webmvc 7.0.9 (Spring Boot 4.1.0) and tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind 3.1.5, per `./gradlew dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath`.

blast_radius.note: Two prod files in one module (Pet.getVisit plus two edit handlers in VisitController) and prose-only doc edits; no sensitive paths. The one hunk that reaches past the new route is the InitBinder allow-list, which also governs the existing booking POST.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every prod hunk: the loader resolves visitId only through the named pet and throws when it is absent, the form posts to its own URL so edits cannot fall through to /visits/new, and the date rule is the booking rule moved into a helper unchanged. The allow-list of date and description also narrows binding on the booking route and on the @ModelAttribute Owner. It closes a pre-existing mass-assignment path, and the design and security records note it, so it is intended rather than hidden. Cosmetic only: the edit page still labels its button Add Visit.

test_adequacy.note: The correction tests are real: a recursive comparison against the corrected visit, a single-element check proving no second visit, no-save checks on refusal, and cross-pet refusal cases, with PetTests covering each getVisit path. But the new setAllowedFields control has no test. No test submits an Owner or extra field on either POST, so removing the allow-list would keep the suite green. The refusal tests also check only that save was never called, not that the visit is unchanged.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers ended approved, and the final doc approval cites VisitController.java:79-80, :124 and :131, which resolve. The parked items are polish: a redundant isNew check, null versus Optional in getVisit, and the amended 2026-08-08 ADR body that still says a booked visit is immutable (line 19). A fix-delta plan scoped out the other floor reviewers in the last round, so their silence is expected.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries, consultations and design revisions. The code matches the REQ-VIS-003 bullets and edge cases, and the NG-5 narrowing plus its ADR follow the intake decision. The booking-route binder change was designed into the triage, not added in a fix round.

rationale: The change is contained and matches its requirement, but read the InitBinder hunk. Its allow-list silently narrows binding on the existing booking route and the Owner attribute, and no test pins it, so a regression would pass green. Consider a tampering test before merge.
